items.claim: I could rely on five of the nine lots: Elbauenpark - Messeparkplatz, Tiefgarage Friedensplatz, Tiefgarage Hotel Maritim, Parkhaus Hotel Ratswaage and Tiefgarage Universitätsplatz.
items.reason: FACTS says 4 of 9 lots were usable—Elbauenpark - Messeparkplatz, Tiefgarage Friedensplatz, Tiefgarage Hotel Maritim and Tiefgarage Ulrichshaus—while Hotel-Ratswaage and Universitaetsplatz had no data.

items.claim: The clearest weekday rhythm was at Tiefgarage Universitätsplatz.
items.reason: Universitaetsplatz was skipped for no data, and the strongest modelled weekday rhythm is at Ulrichshaus (r_squared 0.787).

items.claim: It was quietest in the small hours, mostly around 33% to 39% at 03:00 to 05:00, then climbed through the morning and was usually fullest around 10:00 to 12:00, often between 77.1% and 86.7%.
items.reason: FACTS has no modelled Universitaetsplatz data and does not contain the cited hourly percentages.

items.claim: Tiefgarage Friedensplatz showed a similar shape: low in the late evening and overnight, then strongest around 10:00 to 12:00, with weekday peaks such as 83.3% on 1 September, 82.5% on 10 September and 77.2% on 29 September.
items.reason: FACTS shows a typical weekday trough at 03:00 and peak at 12:00, but it does not contain the cited date-specific percentages.

items.claim: Weekends looked different.
items.reason: FACTS shows mixed lot-level weekend effects, but no single overall weekend statement for parking as a whole.

items.claim: Tiefgarage Universitätsplatz was clearly less full on weekend middays than on weekdays.
items.reason: Universitaetsplatz was skipped for no data, so FACTS does not show any weekend effect for it.

items.claim: On Sundays, it was around 36.5% to 39.9% from 10:00 to 13:00 on 20 and 27 September, while weekday late-morning values were much higher.
items.reason: FACTS has no modelled Universitaetsplatz data and does not contain those date-specific Sunday percentages.

items.claim: Tiefgarage Friedensplatz also ran lower on Sundays: on 20 September it was just 1.3% at 11:00 and 8.8% at 12:00.
items.reason: FACTS shows Friedensplatz's weekend effect is -8.6 points but not significant, and it does not contain the cited 20 September hourly percentages.

items.claim: The exception was Elbauenpark - Messeparkplatz.
items.reason: FACTS does not confirm Elbauenpark as a clear exception: its weekend effect is +6.8 points but not significant.

items.claim: Its weekday pattern was irregular, but its weekend peaks were unmistakable.
items.reason: FACTS shows a low-fit weekday pattern (r_squared 0.25), but its weekend effect is not significant.

items.claim: It reached 97.8% at 11:00 on Saturday 19 September, 98.6% at 11:00 on Sunday 20 September, and 81.1% at 13:00 on Saturday 26 September.
items.reason: FACTS gives only summary values for Elbauenpark, with a typical weekday peak of 38.4% at 11:00 and max 100.0%, not those date-specific figures.

items.claim: Compared with August, I did not see a clear citywide shift in parking at comparable days and hours.
items.reason: Only Friedensplatz is significantly higher month on month; the other three comparable lots show no significant change.

items.claim: The weekday late-morning peak at Universitätsplatz and Friedensplatz remained, and Elbauenpark - Messeparkplatz remained the lot with the strongest weekend surges.
items.reason: Universitaetsplatz was not comparable, Friedensplatz keeps a 12:00 peak, and Elbauenpark's current weekend effect is +6.8 points but not significant.

items.claim: I could use 16 charging stations this month.
items.reason: FACTS list 17 usable charging stations this month, not 16.

items.claim: Occupancy was usually lowest overnight, started to rise after 08:00, and was strongest from about 10:00 to 18:00.
items.reason: The typical weekday profile is lowest overnight, but it is already rising by 07:00 and 08:00, not only after 08:00.

items.claim: Weekends were flatter, with less of the weekday morning ramp and more spread into the afternoon and evening.
items.reason: FACTS give a weekday typical day and per-station weekend effects, but no weekend hourly profile to verify this shape description.

items.claim: Long runs at 50% or 100% were common at some stations, and that fits these reconstructed charging states.
items.reason: FACTS do not record run lengths at 50% or 100%, and the explanation about reconstructed charging states is not stated in FACTS.

items.claim: Against August, I did not see a clear citywide change in charging use.
items.reason: FACTS show mixed station-level month-on-month results, but no citywide aggregate comparison to confirm or deny this.

items.claim: Some stations were fuller at some hours and others were quieter, but the overall daily shape stayed much the same.
items.reason: FACTS show mixed station-level changes, but they do not compare an overall citywide daily shape between months.

items.claim: I could rely on NO2 at City Tunnel, Guericke Strasse, Schleinufer and West, and on O3 at West.
items.reason: Those are the usable NO2 sites and the only usable O3 site.

items.claim: The NO2 pattern on weekdays was the usual road-side one: lowest overnight, then higher in the morning and again from late afternoon into the evening.
items.reason: The fitted weekday NO2 profile is lowest overnight, rises in the morning, and rises again from late afternoon into the evening.

items.claim: The highest hourly values I saw were 118 at City Tunnel, 73 at Guericke Strasse, 89 at Schleinufer and 44 at West.
items.reason: Those are the maximum NO2 values for the four sites.

items.claim: All of these stayed well below the EU hourly NO2 limit of 200.
items.reason: The EU hourly NO2 limit is 200 and all four sites had 0 hours over it.

items.claim: For the WHO daily mean NO2 guideline of 25, I saw exceedances on some days at City Tunnel, and on fewer days at Guericke Strasse and Schleinufer.
items.reason: City Tunnel and Schleinufer each had 11 exceedance days, while Guericke Strasse had 8, so Schleinufer was not on fewer days than City Tunnel.

items.claim: I did not see that at West.
items.reason: West had 1 day over the WHO daily NO2 guideline.

items.claim: O3 at West showed the opposite daily shape: lower in the morning and higher in the late afternoon and early evening.
items.reason: West O3 is lowest in the morning and highest in the late afternoon and early evening.

items.claim: The monthly high was 120 at 18:00 on 28 September.
items.reason: FACTS gives a monthly O3 maximum of 120.0 but does not say it occurred at 18:00 on 28 September.

items.claim: I did not see any breach of the EU 8-hour O3 target of 120.
items.reason: West had 0 days over the EU 8-hour O3 target of 120.

items.claim: The WHO 8-hour O3 guideline of 100 was exceeded on 27 and 30 September.
items.reason: FACTS says the WHO 8-hour O3 guideline was exceeded on 4 days, not just on 27 and 30 September, and does not list all exceedance dates.

items.claim: Compared with August, ozone was clearly lower.
items.reason: West O3 was significantly lower than in August.

items.claim: September peaked at 120, while August reached 173.
items.reason: The September maximum was 120.0 and the August maximum was 173.0.

items.claim: For NO2, I did not see one consistent month-to-month direction across all sites.
items.reason: NO2 month-on-month adjusted shifts were mixed across the four sites, so there was no single direction across all of them.
